storyboard.addedInformation: Names the false model (parallel tracks) the next beats dismantle piece by piece.
storyboard.claim: The brain cannot run the email and the text on parallel tracks.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Everyman at his office desk clutching his buzzing phone, caught mid-glance between laptop and screen.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Picks up the glanced-at text from beat 39 and states the brain fact behind it.

storyboard.addedInformation: Breaks the switch into named mechanical steps, starting with the costly shutdown.
storyboard.claim: Switching starts by disengaging the whole email-writing network at high energy cost.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Earl Miller pointing at the viewer like a lecturer while Everyman sits at his desk behind him, hands frozen over the keyboard.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Zooms from the denial of parallel tracks into step one of what really happens.

storyboard.addedInformation: Shows the second machine spinning up: a fully different comprehension network.
storyboard.claim: The brain must activate completely different networks to read the text.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Close on Everyman's glowing modern smartphone with the incoming text message lit up in his hand.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Step two of the switch: the email machine is off, the text machine powers up.

storyboard.addedInformation: Adds the hidden reassembly cost: tone, sentence position, point — all rebuilt from scratch.
storyboard.claim: Returning means rebooting the email networks and spending energy to find your place again.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Everyman staring back at his half-written email, brow furrowed, phone still in hand, lost mid-sentence.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The round trip completes: text processed, email networks must restart.

storyboard.addedInformation: weak: compresses the factory analogy into a three-step loop the viewer can replay mentally.
storyboard.claim: Every glance is a full shutdown-startup-shutdown-restart cycle, like relighting factory machines.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A three-stage flow loop on screen while Everyman sits idle at his desk behind it, drained by the cycle.
storyboard.onScreenText: The whole cycle, for one glance
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Structural beat: the whole 41-43 mechanism abstracted into one visible loop.

storyboard.addedInformation: Converts the abstract switching cost into bodily fuel the viewer can feel.
storyboard.claim: Each switch burns glucose — real physical metabolic energy.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Earl tapping his temple to make the energy point while Everyman rubs his eyes at the desk.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Puts a fuel gauge on the factory cycle: this is why it exhausts you.

storyboard.addedInformation: weak: gives the phenomenon its official name so the rest of the video can invoke it.
storyboard.claim: Miller's name for this toll is the switching tax, and it produces the screw-up effect.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Earl delivering the verdict straight to camera, Everyman slumped small at the desk beside him.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The mechanism earns its name: the tax label lands on everything since beat 40.

storyboard.addedInformation: Explains why errors multiply: the manager is exhausted before the work begins.
storyboard.claim: Energy spent managing transitions leaves less energy for the work itself.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Earl counting off on his fingers while Everyman holds his head, mid-mistake, behind him.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Consequence one of the tax: the transition overhead eats the work budget.

storyboard.addedInformation: Makes the impairment bodily: spiking error, lagging reactions, dulled competence.
storyboard.claim: Taxed brains show spiking error rates, slower reactions, and measurably worse competence.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Everyman collapsed over his keyboard, typo-ridden email on screen, too fried to fix it.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Consequence two: the degraded output of the depleted brain, shown not told.

storyboard.addedInformation: States the control condition the science compares against: single-task, finish, then move.
storyboard.claim: Doing one task fully before moving on beats every juggling attempt.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Everyman pausing, one finished email sent, finger hovering calmly over the next — the alternative.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The baseline the whole tax argument rests on: finish, then move.

storyboard.addedInformation: Introduces the lay host's lived objection that the next beats will dismantle.
storyboard.claim: The host confesses he genuinely feels like a skilled multitasker in his own life.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Johann Hari speaking with easy confidence, slightly smiling — a man sure he can juggle.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Turn from lab science to personal testimony: the objection the viewer shares.

storyboard.addedInformation: Stages the exact lived scenario: podcast plus routine email, camera off, fingers typing.
storyboard.claim: Podcast-plus-email feels like two separate bandwidths that should not collide.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Everyman at his desk with earbuds in, phone glowing beside the laptop, typing through a meeting.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The objection made concrete: the desk scene every viewer recognizes.

storyboard.addedInformation: Sharpens the objection into anatomy: ears versus eyes-plus-fingers.
storyboard.claim: Audio in the ears and typing under the fingers seem like non-overlapping channels.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Everyman touching one earbud with one hand while the other hand keeps typing — two channels, seemingly.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The strongest version of the illusion, staged as body parts that feel independent.

storyboard.addedInformation: Poses the honest question that hands the floor back to the neuroscience.
storyboard.claim: The host asks whether the brain truly shuts down or just uses separate channels.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Johann leaning in, eyebrows raised, asking the question straight at Earl across the conversation.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The challenge issued: separate channels or shutdown — the expert must answer.

storyboard.addedInformation: Names the trap: the seamlessness is manufactured by the brain papering over gaps.
storyboard.claim: Feeling simultaneous is the exact illusion — the brain hides the gaps from you.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The narrator warning to camera while Everyman behind her smiles on, oblivious, mid-juggle.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The verdict on the objection: what felt like skill was a cover-up.

storyboard.addedInformation: Gives the anatomical reason the illusion must fail: one shared executive gate.
storyboard.claim: Neurologically a central bottleneck binds both tasks no matter the senses used.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Earl holding up one finger — one gate — while Everyman's earbuds and keyboard sit uselessly on either side.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The mechanism behind the illusion: separate ears, single gate.

storyboard.addedInformation: Locates the collision precisely in semantic processing, not in the senses.
storyboard.claim: Both listening and typing demand the same executive network to process word meaning.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Earl tapping his forehead where meaning gets made, mid-lecture, eyes locked on the viewer.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Narrows the bottleneck to its exact site: meaning, not sound or touch.

storyboard.addedInformation: Sets up the collision experiment: complex Zoom sentence versus complex email sentence.
storyboard.claim: Two complex meanings arriving together cannot both be processed at once.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Earl grave and direct while Everyman freezes between his ringing meeting and his half-typed sentence.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The stress test: what happens when both channels demand meaning at once.

storyboard.addedInformation: Shows the real behavior: rapid toggling with fragments silently lost from each stream.
storyboard.claim: The brain toggles frantically between streams, dropping bits of each unnoticed.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Split screen: Everyman's earbud audio stream on one side, his email text on the other, fragments visibly falling out between them.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The answer to beat 57's question: toggling, not sharing — staged as two leaking streams.

storyboard.addedInformation: Reveals the cover-up artist: predictive models forging a seamlessness that never happened.
storyboard.claim: You miss the losses because predictive models fill the blanks into fake seamlessness.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Everyman calm, almost serene at his desk — composed face above a screen full of holes he cannot see.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The calm-after-toggling irony: his peace is the forgery, staged as a placid face over damage.

storyboard.addedInformation: States the price of the forgery: depth traded for the feeling of efficiency.
storyboard.claim: Micro-switching means doing both jobs badly while sacrificing real depth.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A single dimming lightbulb idea guttering above Everyman's slumped shoulders at the desk.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The bill for the fake seamlessness: two degraded jobs, one starved idea.

storyboard.addedInformation: Names what fragments can never build: background associative links of deep thought.
storyboard.claim: Original thought needs sustained attention so the brain can link ideas in the background.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Everyman staring past his screen, trying to hold one thought still while notifications crowd the frame.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: What was sacrificed in beat 60, specified: the slow background linking work.

storyboard.addedInformation: Closes the switching-tax arc: gear-grinding plus error-correction consumes the whole budget.
storyboard.claim: Power spent switching and fixing toggle-errors leaves nothing for deep thought.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Everyman emptied over his desk, screen glaring, hands limp — the tank visibly on zero.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The arc's endpoint: the taxed brain from beat 48, now fully drained.

storyboard.addedInformation: Reframes interruptions as violence against thought's natural flow, not mere delays.
storyboard.claim: We constantly dam our thoughts' natural current for artificial interruptions.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Everyman jerking upright at each buzz, his unfolding thought visibly snapping mid-thread.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: From mechanism to habit: the repeated stopping summarized as a way of life.

storyboard.addedInformation: weak: plants the river image the rest of the video will tax, bottle, and sell back.
storyboard.claim: The switching tax is a toll booth built mid-river in your river of attention.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A wide river of attention with a stark toll booth barred across its middle, Everyman stalled before it.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The whole tax argument crystallized into one landscape image.

storyboard.addedInformation: Pivots the stakes from productivity to profundity: what dies is experience itself.
storyboard.claim: Constant stopping makes us casualties of flow — denied a profound human experience.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The narrator grave to camera, naming the casualty while the river image fades behind her.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: From the toll booth to its true cost: not output, but the loss of flow.

storyboard.addedInformation: Bridges from theory to origin story: to grasp flow, travel somewhere unexpected and dark.
storyboard.claim: Understanding flow means traveling to a completely different, grim scene.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The narrator turning, gesturing into darkness as the office world falls away behind her.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The pivot staged as a journey: leave the desk, enter the past.

storyboard.addedInformation: Establishes the extremity that proves the point: if peace is possible here, the mechanism is fundamental.
storyboard.claim: A freezing, starvation-ravaged World War II gulag of malnutrition and despair.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The narrator small against a bleak frozen camp landscape, breath visible, an unbroken chain across the frozen ground, delivering the horror plainly.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Arrival at the grim scene promised: cold, hunger, and dying all around.

storyboard.addedInformation: Introduces Moric through his famous brother, linking the camp to the psychology to come.
storyboard.claim: Among the prisoners is Moric, brother of the future flow psychologist Mihaly Csikszentmihalyi.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The narrator telling the story with the warm older psychologist Mihaly listening beside her, head bowed.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: A face in the camp crowd: the prisoner whose story carries the theory.

storyboard.addedInformation: Completes the identification: the broken prisoner is kin to the century's flow authority.
storyboard.claim: Moric is physically broken and has lost everything; Mihaly will become the father of flow.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The narrator in the frozen camp, small against the ice, plainly reporting the ruin of a man who has lost everything.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The lowest point held on screen so the coming peace lands with full force.

storyboard.addedInformation: Plants the humble trigger of transcendence: a crystal found in the mud.
storyboard.claim: Amidst suffering Moric finds peace through a shimmering crystal-like rock.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The narrator small in the camp darkness, one hand out toward a small crystal-studded stone on the frozen ground, a glint of gold light off its points.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The turn: one small glimmer inside total darkness.

storyboard.addedInformation: Shows expertise becoming refuge: geology training focusing a starving mind.
storyboard.claim: His geology past lets him intensely study the rock's composition and structure.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The narrator beside the same stone, reporting how a geology background let the prisoner read the rock's chemistry in its facets.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The mechanism of the peace: trained attention locking onto the stone.

storyboard.addedInformation: States flow's signature erasure without staging the camp's horrors as spectacle.
storyboard.claim: Lost in facets and light, the cold, hunger, and gulag simply vanish for a moment.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Mihaly absorbed, gaze fused to the stone, the bleak camp dissolved out of the frame around him.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The payoff of the camp story: total absorption erasing total suffering.

storyboard.addedInformation: Translates the extreme case into a modern one every creative viewer knows.
storyboard.claim: The same mechanism appears in a modern painter losing the day in the studio.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The narrator presenting the modern parallel, brushstroke-lit studio warmth replacing camp cold.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: From the extreme proof back to ordinary life: the same state, a safe studio.

storyboard.addedInformation: Details the trance markers: skipped meals, lost hours, sweat, hypnotic merger.
storyboard.claim: Eight to six vanishes unfelt — no food, no bathroom, merged with the canvas.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The narrator describing the trance while an unseen painter's canvas fills the frame, hours implied, body forgotten.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The modern flow portrait painted in full: time and body gone, only work left.

storyboard.addedInformation: Stages the paradox without triumph: the finished work abandoned proves the state was the prize.
storyboard.claim: Finished, the painting is put away — the product never mattered.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The narrator turning away mid-gesture as the finished canvas is leaned against a wall, walked past, forgotten.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The twist that redefines the trance: its goal was never the painting.

storyboard.addedInformation: Explicitly rejects the product reading so no viewer mistakes flow for productivity.
storyboard.claim: It was never about the final product — only the psychological state of making it.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The narrator crossing out the very idea of the product, the abandoned canvas small in the corner.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The rejection beat: the product crossed out, the state left standing.

storyboard.addedInformation: Gives the state its name and restates the stakes: fragmentation blocks deep living.
storyboard.claim: Mihaly named that state flow — and fragmentation stops us living deeply.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Mihaly bright and certain, naming his life's discovery straight to the viewer.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The naming beat: camp rock and studio canvas unified under one word.

storyboard.addedInformation: Makes flow a need, not a luxury: meaning and texture depend on it.
storyboard.claim: Fulfillment — a life with meaning and texture — requires flow states.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Mihaly warm and affirming beside the nodding narrator: this is about a life worth living.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: From definition to human stakes: why the viewer should care about flow.

storyboard.addedInformation: Defines flow's phenomenology positively as merger, not as the vanishing of negatives.
storyboard.claim: In flow, time falls away, the inner critic and ego dissolve into the task.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Mihaly serene and absorbed, gaze steady, the world narrowed to one luminous point of work.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The portrait completed: what flow feels like from the inside, held on a calm face.
